Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pnrr 0.1.0

  • First version. clean_cpr(), add_cpr_info() and age() moved here from daos, with their native C kernel, tests and benchmarks. daos no longer has them and does not forward to pnrr.

  • age() is now age_at(ref, at). The reference is one argument, and its type decides what it is: whole numbers are years, a Date or an ISO date string is a date. age(date = x) is age_at(x). The primo argument is gone: age(year, primo = "jan1") is age_at(year, "jan1"), and "primo" is always 31 December of the year before, as it was by default. cpr_age(x, ref, at) has the same form. age(...) in add_cpr_info() gives an error that shows the new form; bare age still means today’s age. The name says what the argument is: age() looked like it calculated an age.

  • add_cpr_info() gains the status selection, and cpr_status() is its vector version: a factor that says for each row why a value is or is not valid, with the problems of diagnose_cpr() as levels. The two share one classification and cannot disagree.

  • add_cpr_info() gains the koen selection, and cpr_koen() is its vector version: sex coded 1 for men and 2 for women, as KOEN in the registers of Statistics Denmark. sex is still 1 and 0.

  • diagnose_cpr() reports what is wrong with a CPR column: missing values, scientific notation, wrong lengths, other characters and invalid dates, with notes on restored leading zeros, separators, modulus 11, repeated values and implausible birth dates. It prints counts and row numbers, never CPR numbers.

  • cpr_birth_date(), cpr_birth_year(), cpr_sex(), cpr_valid(), cpr_mod11() and cpr_age() give one piece of information as a vector, for mutate() and filter(). They return exactly what the matching add_cpr_info() selection does, from the same native code.

  • add_cpr_info() gains the byear selection, the birth year as an integer. It is not among the defaults, so default output is unchanged, and the native pass is as fast as before.

  • add_cpr_info()’s arguments are now .data, .cpr_col and .overwrite. An output name such as d = bday or cpr = age_at(year) was partially matched to data or cpr_col and gave a misleading error. The old names give an error that points to the new ones.

  • diagnose_cpr() classifies in one native pass: about four times faster, one second for five million values.

  • pseudo_cpr() replaces CPR numbers with serial numbers in random order. The same CPR number gets the same serial number within a call; no key is kept. The documentation now says that a seed is a secret: with it, the serial numbers can be traced back to the order of the source.

  • Cleaning also removes the separators that cannot be seen: tabs, line breaks, no-break spaces and typographic dashes, such as the en dash Word makes of a hyphen. They were reported as non_digit and made a valid number invalid. This applies everywhere CPR numbers are read.

  • clean_cpr() gives an error for a data frame or a list, as the other vector functions do, instead of returning a deparsed string.

  • add_cpr_info() and the cpr_*() functions read CPR numbers stored as numbers directly, without converting each to text first: about 25 times faster on a numeric column, 0.3 seconds for ten million values. A year reference is validated in the native code: age_at(year) on a column is about a third faster, and three ages in one call more than twice as fast.

  • Whole numbers that R writes in scientific notation, such as 1010000000 ("1.01e+09"), keep their digits everywhere. They were read as malformed, and diagnose_cpr() reported them as lost digits.

  • add_cpr_info() returns a data.table that can be modified with := without the shallow-copy warning.

Developed by Daniel Madsen.
